title: Fleet Admission Sieve: per-tenant micro-quotas and latency-tail shedding
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a modular admission 'sieve' in the dedicated routing path that enforces fine-grained micro-quotas, provides a bounded slowpath queue, and performs latency-tail-aware shedding. This ticket covers spec, implementation plan, and rollout for the runtime + control-plane changes needed to guarantee per-tenant throughput commitments while protecting node-level latency SLOs during overload events.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant baseline throughput guarantees enforced: tenants with reserved capacity see >= 95% of committed throughput under typical load patterns (validated in load tests)
Tail latency protection: P99 token generation latency for high-priority customers does not regress more than 10% during synthetic overload compared to baseline
Overload behaviour: under 2x-peak stress test, total error rate due to admission rejection or shedding remains < 3% for P0/P1 customers and < 8% for best-effort customers
Autoscaler integration: admission controller exposes headroom hints and burst-credit consumption metrics consumed by the Dedicated autoscaler (end-to-end validation in staging)
Observability: new dashboards for per-tenant tokens, slowpath queue depth, shed events, and borrowing rates are present and alerting thresholds configured
implementation_plan: Design a lightweight admission sieve component that composes token buckets at three dimensions: tenant, model, and node-slot
Add a bounded slowpath queue module to the router: fixed-size ring buffer with backpressure indicators and per-request timestamps
Implement latency-tail detector that marks high-tail candidates (based on recent P95/P99 history) and tags requests for fastpath prioritization
Expose admission metrics (tokens granted, tokens denied, queue enqueue/dequeue, queue drops, tail-tags) via Prometheus and per-tenant telemetry streams
Add control-plane APIs to configure micro-quota policies, burst credits, and priority classes for Dedicated customers
Hook admission headroom hints into existing autoscaler controller: define hint contract and add unit tests and e2e test harness
Unit + integration tests: token correctness, borrow/repay semantics, queue edge conditions, and failure injection
testing_plan: Create synthetic workload generator that can vary short-term QPS and burst patterns across tenants and models
Run canary load tests in staging with a mix of reserved and best-effort tenants to validate throughput guarantees and shedding thresholds
Chaos testing: simulate node failure and degraded network to ensure admission sieve gracefully adapts without violating high-priority contracts
Compare latencies (P50/P95/P99) vs baseline for a representative production trace replay
Automated regression suite added to CI for core admission properties (no regressions on token leakage or unlimited borrowing)
monitoring_and_observability: Dashboard: Dedicated > Admission Sieve showing: per-tenant tokens/sec, queue depth/time-in-queue, shed-rate, borrow-credits-remaining
Alert: sustained queue depth > 80% capacity for 5m -> paging SRE
Alert: P99 latency for P0 customers increased > 20% over baseline for 10m
Log enrichment: admission events include tenant_id, model_id, request_id, token_reason, and decision (fastpath/slowpath/shed)
Expose new metrics to billing pipeline to ensure denied requests do not count towards customer usage
rollout_plan: Alpha: enable admission sieve with conservative defaults for 3 internal tenants in us-west-2 (2 weeks)
Beta: onboarding script for 10 pilot customers with configurable micro-quotas and burst credits (4 weeks)
Canary: 5% traffic on Dedicated fleets with observability gating and automatic rollback on error budget burn
Gradual ramp with config-driven exemptions and real-time adjustments via control plane UI
Full: flip default enforcement for best-effort lanes after 6 weeks and iterate policy knobs per tenant feedback
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: over-aggressive shedding could cause unexpected client errors -> mitigation: start with sampling-only mode and circuit-breaker for auto-rollback
Risk: token accounting drift across nodes under partial failures -> mitigation: idempotent grant/consume operations and reconciliation job that runs periodically
Risk: autoscaler misinterprets headroom hints leading to thrashing -> mitigation: smoothing window on hints and rate-limit scale decisions
Risk: added routing latency from sieve checks -> mitigation: micro-optimized hot path and fastpath bypass for explicitly privileged tenants
